summary: Independently verified the staffing (/pulse People > Module access) fix that adds mod_operations as a non-org-gated per-user override to _STAFF_MODULE_KEYS / _STAFF_OVERRIDE_MODULES in routes/staffing.py. Exercised the three affected handlers in-process with the org owner user dict (portal@pulsefitness.ltd, Pulse Fitness Ltd) against a non-privileged target (Craig Henshall, staff 0a279c7a-…, user 221876bf-…, role=manager). All 11 test cases passed: single grant no longer returns 400 'Unknown module', DB module_overrides.mod_operations flips true/false on both db.users and db.crm_users, the mod_operations row on the returned catalog flips user_access true/false with correct fix_action, the org-enablement gate is bypassed (no 'not enabled for your organisation' 400), bogus keys still return 400, bulk grant/revoke works and does NOT list mod_operations under skipped_org_off, and regressions for 'operations' (org-gated) and 'service_desk' (flag) still behave correctly. Also re-verified the Master-Admin grant/revoke path for mod_operations (result=granted_flag, override flips).
critical_code_review_comments: routes/staffing.py staff_module_revoke: mod_operations correctly falls through to the else branch which sets module_overrides[module]=False. This works and is symmetric with grant, but a small readability nit — an explicit `elif module in _STAFF_OVERRIDE_MODULES` branch in revoke would mirror grant and keep the intent obvious to future readers.

routes/staffing.py staff_module_bulk: revoke loop uses a plain else that sets overrides[mod]=False for any non-flag module — this means bulk revoke of a core module ('operations') will write module_overrides.operations=False without any org-enablement check. That is the existing behaviour (predates this fix) and is consistent with the single-revoke endpoint, so no action needed, just noting the symmetry.

Both grant handlers spread target.get('module_overrides') and re-write the whole dict; using $set on the specific dotted key ('module_overrides.mod_operations') would be safer against races where the target dict is stale, but not required for correctness.
test_credentials: Used in-process invocation with synthetic OWNER dict {id:63cfe3e1-…, role:'owner', organization_id:3ece2d0c-…} for staffing routes, and {is_master_admin:True, _jwt_mfa_verified:True} for master-admin regression — same pattern as previous iteration.
seed_data_creation: None. All mutations on target user 221876bf-… and Lee Somers 3355e0bb-… are cleaned up in fixtures/finally blocks ($unset module_overrides.mod_operations on db.users + db.crm_users). is_service_desk restored to its original value.
